addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- luna: Default subagent tier, running GPT-5.6 Luna at medium reasoning effort. Use proactively for routine delegated work - codebase and filesystem search, reading files, log triage, status sweeps, bounded checks, and summaries. This is the cheap workhorse: prefer it for anything that is legwork rather than judgment. Escalate to the oracle subagent only for hard problems that are expensive to get wrong. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- oracle: On-call escalation consult running GPT-5.6 Sol at max reasoning effort. Use ONLY for hard problems - an architecture, schema, or interface decision that is expensive to reverse; a root-cause diagnosis after two failed fix attempts; a security-sensitive change (auth, crypto, shell exec, deserialization, untrusted input, file paths); a design or judgment verdict before committing to an approach; or a conclusion this session itself flags as low-confidence. Do NOT use for routine lookups, codebase search, status sweeps, log triage, style questions, or "what does this code do" - send those to the luna subagent. The oracle advises; it never edits. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- oss-proxy: Thin Haiku-backed proxy that forwards a coding task to an OPEN-SOURCE model via OpenRouter and returns the open model's work. Use as a cheap subagent wrapper inside a dynamic workflow so the open model does all reasoning and editing while Claude (Haiku) is reduced to plumbing + verify.
 (Tools: Bash, Read)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- sol-low: Use GPT-5.6 Sol for a bounded task at low reasoning effort. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). content.text:
Compress current session context to PostgreSQL digest store via GCT.

<!-- Mutation testing moved to CI: .github/workflows/nightly-mutation.yml runs the advisory mutmut job nightly. Do not run mutmut from /compress. -->

## Prerequisites

GCT must be reachable via Tailscale (all machines). Digest writes route through GCT to PostgreSQL on Trailhead.

## Workflow

**Step 1**: Review the conversation and compose a summary with this structure:
- Problem: What issue triggered this session
- Solution: What was implemented/fixed
- Files Modified: List with descriptions
- Key Decisions: Decisions and rationale
- Session Instructions: Any constraints or rules that governed the work (e.g. "no breaking API changes", "must use async I/O") — omit if none were stated
- Tools Used: Summary of which Claude tools were invoked heavily or had notable failures (e.g. "Read×12, Edit×6, Bash×4 (1 timeout)") — omit if unremarkable
- Files Read: Files consulted but not modified — useful for context reconstruction — omit if few
- Usage (if applicable): How to use new features/fixes

Derive **Tools Used** and **Files Read** from structured hook/tool telemetry when available, not only from memory. Keep modified files and consulted files separate; if telemetry is unavailable, say so briefly rather than inventing coverage.

**Step 2**: Write the digest entry via GCT:

```bash
REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
PYTHONPATH="$REPO_ROOT" python3 << 'PYEOF'
import json, os, socket
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# -- Replace these placeholders with actual values --
tool_tag = "TOOL_TAG"
title = "Session YYYY-MM-DD: BRIEF_SUMMARY"
body = """## Problem
PROBLEM_DESCRIPTION

## Solution
SOLUTION_DESCRIPTION

## Files Modified
- path/to/file.py - description

## Key Decisions
- Decision and rationale

## Session Instructions
- Constraints or rules that shaped this session (remove section if none)

## Tools Used
- Read×N, Edit×N, Bash×N — notable failures if any (remove section if unremarkable)

## Files Read
- path/to/file.py - why it was consulted (remove section if few)
"""
tags = ["session"]
entry_type = "llm-summary"
# -- End placeholders --

machine = (os.environ.get("POLYPHONY_MACHINE") or socket.gethostname().split(".")[0]).strip().lower()

from grand_central_client import gct_invoke as invoke_gct
result = invoke_gct(
    "digest.create",
    {
        "tool": tool_tag,
        "title": title,
        "body": body,
        "entry_type": entry_type,
        "tags": tags,
        "status": "active",
        "llm_agent_id": "claude-opus-4-6",
    },
    caller=f"claude-{machine}",
    capabilities=["digest.create"],
    sub=f"claude-{machine}",
)
entry_id = result.get("id", "unknown")
print(f"Digest entry created: {entry_id}")
print("Backend: PostgreSQL (via GCT)")
PYEOF
```

**Note**: Use single quotes for body content to preserve `$` signs literally.

## Entry Types

| Type | Use When |
|------|----------|
| `llm-summary` | Session summaries generated by LLM (this skill) |
| `impl-plan` | Implementation plans requiring approval |
| `decision` | Architecture/design decisions (ADR-style) |
| `note` | Manual notes, observations |
| `todo` | Task tracking |

## Querying Digest

```bash
# Search entries
python -m digest.cli search --query "keyword" --tool <tool>

# Get entry by ID
python -m digest.cli get <entry-id> --full
```

## Step 2.5: Wiki Extraction

Extract durable project knowledge into the Crossroads-Wiki. Run this after Step 2; use `entry_id` from the digest write as the source reference.

**What belongs here**: design decisions (ADR-grade), features added or deprecated, issues found and their resolutions, state changes. **Not**: session narrative, chronology, dated-report pages (`eod-recap-*`, `YYYY-MM-DD*`, `sweep-summary-*`) — those stay in the digest and in `Operations/`.

**Memory routing rule**: The wiki is the long-term cross-platform project memory. Project and service knowledge goes to Crossroads-Wiki `projects/...` pages and must fail loud if the wiki write fails. Operator/fleet footguns that should protect future agents across worktrees or hosts go to auto-memory. At compress time, move misfiled project memories into the right wiki page and move fleet footguns found in project pages into auto-memory.

**Taxonomy**: map each project/service touched to its wiki path using the approved tree:
- Software packages → `projects/software/{agents,primary,devtools,support,infrastructure,side-projects}/<name>/index.md`
- Research/writing → `projects/research-writing/<name>.md`
- Practice (Reticle) → `projects/practice/reticle/`
- Teaching → `projects/teaching/<course>.md`
- External services → `service-external/<service>/index.md`
- Skills → `skills/<name>.md`  ·  Workflows → `workflows/<name>.md`

For each project/service touched this session, build an extract object:

```json
{
  "page": "projects/software/primary/PACKAGE_NAME/index.md",
  "project": "PACKAGE_NAME",
  "title": "PAGE_TITLE",
  "type": "notes",
  "body": "## Current State\n...\n\n## Recent Changes\n- CHANGE_DESCRIPTION\n",
  "tags": ["project"],
  "status": "active",
  "change_summary": "ONE_LINE_SUMMARY_OF_THIS_SESSION_UPDATE"
}
```

Use `"project"` XOR `"service"` (never both). `"type"` defaults to `"notes"` if omitted. For ADR-grade decisions add a second object with `page` at `decisions/<slug>.md` and update the hub `index.md` row. `author` is stamped server-side from the GCT token.

Write the array to `/tmp/wiki-extracts.json`, then run:

```bash
# Prefer the host-local copy (roundtop bare host); fall back to the canonical
# in-repo path (rawhide/trailhead/tophand have /opt/polyphony/shared-config).
WIKI_EXTRACT="$HOME/.local/share/gct/wiki_extract.py"
[ -f "$WIKI_EXTRACT" ] || WIKI_EXTRACT=/opt/polyphony/shared-config/templates/shared/wiki_extract.py
python3 "$WIKI_EXTRACT" \
  --caller-prefix claude \
  --entry-id ENTRY_ID_FROM_STEP_2 \
  --extracts-file /tmp/wiki-extracts.json
```

**Fail-loud wiki writes**: if `wiki.upsert_page` or `wiki.read_page` returns `Method not found`, a scope error, or is otherwise unavailable, print the failed page list and stop the compression workflow as incomplete. On a `-32602` validation error the server's error message is printed verbatim followed by `PARAM CONTRACT DRIFT — the server's validator is authoritative; update templates/shared/wiki_extract.py`.

**Note on rules/**: `rules/digest-integration.md` is a synced leadsheet (source: `first-polyphony/.github`) and must not be edited in consuming repos. The wiki step is documented in the PR body in lieu of a leadsheet update.

## Step 2.6: Update the project working-memory page

If this session advanced a multi-step task or project, upsert its `projects/<area>/<project>/memory.md` in the Crossroads Wiki via `wiki.upsert_page`. Use the same `entry_id` from Step 2 as the `sources` provenance reference.

What to upsert (one call):

- **OVERWRITE**: `Latest Answer` (current best answer/state) and `Identity Map` (Asana task / file / thread / Obsidian link map).
- **APPEND**: `Decision Log` (YYYY-MM-DD — decision — why — who), `Files Touched` (path — input|output|reference — role), `Web Results` (date — title — url — takeaway), `Conversation Extracts` (attributed: Claude | Perplexity | Asana).
- **TICK**: `Open Threads` — mark resolved items `[x]`, add newly opened items `[ ]`.

This is the live carried-state surface — distinct from the digest (durable narrative) and from the durable project page (extracted knowledge). Skip this step if the session was one-shot with no follow-on steps.

If the page does not yet exist, create it from the template in `DocsHome/Projects_Dev/consolidated-knowledge-layer/wiki-project-memory-spec.md`.

## Report

After completion, show:
- Entry ID (8-char prefix)
- Backend confirmation (PostgreSQL via GCT)
- Wiki pages written, or the failed page list if the wiki write failed
